### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9987d45bd56cc1c121ac2ca6cad0daf075ea0344` — the merge of head `543a53e54b37c0a6729a4234159511e3a6dea0dc` into base `80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9987d45bd56cc1c121ac2ca6cad0daf075ea0344 && git checkout 9987d45bd56cc1c121ac2ca6cad0daf075ea0344
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172 543a53e54b37c0a6729a4234159511e3a6dea0dc && git checkout -B drift-repro 80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172 && git merge --no-ff 543a53e54b37c0a6729a4234159511e3a6dea0dc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 80cdbd4e0fe293696ab2ada350b5b348ff4ed172` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read) · Head-sha: f54ec13b444d4a671865a641dbbe8d07896fb686 · 2026-11-16T13:49Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, on the final head declared in 6918245890. I read card #34336, the scope note 6917833544, dev report 6917684209, and the full diff against merge base `719b6b53` (4 commits, 3 files, +363/−18). No L2 is owed: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR is not governed.

- **Card relation.** The PR body says `Fixes #34336`. Card ask 1 (install and reseed read every package body, in package order) is built here. Ask 2 (an upgrade replays new seed keys into existing organizations) is not built here; it moved to #34405 and #34406 by scope note 6917833544. Same-family findings are on #34407. So `Fixes` closes the card on ask 1 with ask 2 carried elsewhere. The area should confirm that the card's done condition reads that way, or say so on the card when it closes.
- **One reader.** `seedDatasetsOf(body)` = `resolveStackCollection(body, 'data')` from `@objectstack/core` (`stack-collections.ts`), filtered to entries that have an `object` and `records`.
  - The top-level `data` wins whenever it is present, so a flat bundle, or a composed artifact that still carries the flattened union, is read once and never again per package. Otherwise each package body is read in `packages[]` order.
  - On this head, `git grep` in `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` finds no `manifest.data` / `converted.data` read left.
  - Every door goes through `seedDatasetsOf`: install, reseed and upgrade (`applySideEffects`), the rehydrate share and heal (`maybeHealSampleData`), purge, the sample-data count, and the listing's `withSampleData`.
- **Pins.** The new test file `marketplace-install-local-composed-bundle-seeds.test.ts` pins:
  - install, with core seeded before the module that depends on it and the datasets shared for new organizations;
  - reseed;
  - an upgrade that adds a package;
  - count and purge;
  - the listing;
  - a restart, both sharing and healing.

  Its three controls are: a flat bundle unchanged, a composed artifact with a flattened `data` read once, and a composed artifact with no datasets still answering `no-datasets`. Per 6917684209 the file was red on base (6 failed, controls green) and is 9/9 at head.
- **Changeset.** `patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection`. Each door it names matches a call site above.
  - The upgrade paragraph ("seeds the incoming version's datasets into the organization the request acts in … other organizations are not reseeded") states the flat-bundle behaviour, unchanged, and that matches the code.
  - It does not promise ask 2.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 51 names, 35 success, 16 skipped (path-filtered, opt-in and queue-only), 0 failed, 0 pending.
- **Base.** PRBASE = `162fe54f` (Test Core plan, `Affected-set diff base`), so K = 4 to `origin/main`, below 15. Nothing since touches `cloud-connection/**` or `stack-collections.ts`. The planned merge of `origin/main` after p0 #34397 comes back to me as a merge-only delta.

### Should (not blocking)

- **The purge and count doors do not catch the reader's refusal.** `seedDatasetsOf` can now throw: `stackPackageBodies` raises the ADR-0112 refusal for a malformed `packages`. Three doors catch it and say why: the heal (warn, then skip), the listing (warn, then `withSampleData: false`) and `applySideEffects` (`seed-datasets-unread` in the summary). But `handlePurge` (`seedDatasetsOf(entry.manifest)`, around line 6068) and `handleSampleDataCount` (around line 6369) call it bare, so a ledger body with a malformed `packages` reaches the route's error path instead of an answer that names the entry.
  - It is not reachable through install, because the `manifest` service refuses those bytes first. Only a hand-edited or older ledger body could carry them.
  - Either route both doors through the same reason the reseed gives for an unreadable entry (`unreadableLedgerEntry`), with a pin, or record it in `## Acceptance notes` as accepted.

Landing: not Tier H. After the merge-only delta (if it comes) is read, area o1-B lands it.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, delta) · Head-sha: 543a53e54b37c0a6729a4234159511e3a6dea0dc · 2026-11-16T15:36Z

This is L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, reading the final head declared in 6920968387. It is a delta read against my ACCEPT 6918284604 at `f54ec13b`. The delta has two parts: the merge of `origin/main` as `9e67ea6c`, and fix commit `543a53e5` (3 files, +80/−2).

- **Merge `9e67ea6c`: clean and mechanical.** Since the previous merge base, no file changed on both sides. Relative to main's parent, the merge carries only this PR's three files (the changeset, the plugin and the pin file).
- **My Should is closed.**
  - The purge (`handlePurge`) and the count (`handleSampleDataCount`) now read a ledger entry's datasets through `ledgerSeedDatasets`. When the resolver refuses the body, that helper catches the refusal and answers `unreadableLedgerEntry`, the same answer these doors already give an entry that fails to read. That answer names the ledger file and quotes the cause, and nothing is deleted.
  - `LocalManifestSource.fileNameOf` returns the on-disk basename (`safeFilename`), spelled the way `SkippedManifestEntry.file` spells it.
  - Pins: the purge and the count, run over a ledger body whose `packages` is `'not-a-list'`, each answer `500 MARKETPLACE_STORAGE_FAILED` with the file name in the message. The purge pin also asserts nothing reached the purge (`purgeCalls` is empty). The area records both pins as red before the fix.
  - The other three doors (heal, listing, `applySideEffects`) are unchanged from my earlier read, so all five readers of `seedDatasetsOf` now handle a refusal.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 55 names, 36 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed, 1 still running (`Check Changeset`) when I read them. Landing needs it green.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `80cdbd4e` (Test Core plan, `Affected-set diff base`), so K = 5 to `origin/main`. Nothing since then touches `cloud-connection/**` or `stack-collections.ts`.

Landing: not Tier H, and no L2 is owed. Area o1-B lands it once `Check Changeset` is green.
